No card: this PR carries none by rule. Inputs were the PR body, its 26-path file list, the net diff against merge base `7de1bad5cbf`, and the check-runs on this head. At the time of reading, the check-runs that had concluded were all success or skipped (Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, PR-body guards, Build Docs); Test Core 1–10, Test UI 1–16, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates and the two E2E jobs were still in progress and carry no conclusion yet. This record judges the contract; those conclusions remain the queue's to read.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of a completed reset, widened by two row families — right. `endWhatTheAccountRegistered` reads `sys_oauth_application` by `user_id` with `disabled` false or null and writes `disabled: true` with the whole-second `updated_at`, the same two columns and the same system context the `/admin/oauth2/toggle-disabled` mount writes; it reads `sys_scim_connection_credential` by `user_id` with `active: true` and revokes each through `revokeScimConnectionCredential`, the function the admin revoke door calls. All four reset doors reach the one arm: both self-service doors through `endWhatTheAccountAddedBeforeAReset` in the after-hook, the forced reset and the operator's through `revokeSessionsAndApiKeys`. The routine forced reset (`revokeSessionsAndKeys: false`) never calls it.
- Owner scoping — right. The only ownership key read is `user_id` equal to a non-empty account id (the after-hook refuses an unnamed subject, the forced path returns early on an empty id, the operator's id comes from the found account), so a row with a null owner can never match, and `reference_id` is never consulted. Neither object carries an organization column that the read could cross: an account's registrations are the account's wherever they sit, which is what the rule says. Both `user_id` columns are indexed.
- What a disabled app is refused — right, on the evidence in the diff. `mcpConsentAdmits` answers false for a client whose `disabled` is truthy before it looks at any consent, so the MCP door refuses every grant type's token, consent-less clients included. The token endpoint and introspection are the vendor's; the new test drives the real provider through `handleRequest` and pins `invalid_client` on a client-credentials grant and a not-active introspection answer after the reset, with a before-control. The vendor source is not in this read-only tree, so that part rests on the test and its check-run, not on a read of the vendor.
- Kept set — right. `sys_sso_provider` and the second-factor rows are only read (`whatAResetKeeps`), never written; the test compares the stored rows before and after.
- Public surface, additive — right. `data.revoked.ownedApps` / `scimCredentials`, ledger keys `revokedOwnedApps` / `revokedScimCredentials`, `ownedAppsDisabled` / `scimCredentialsRevoked` on the operator outcome, a new built-in template name `auth.password_reset_notice` (four locales) added to `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE`, and four new required variables on `auth.password_changed_notice`. No `packages/spec` schema names any of these keys. The exact-shape assertions in `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts` and the dogfood ledger pin were moved with the shape.
- Template variables — one consequence worth naming: a deployment that overrides `auth.password_changed_notice` keeps rendering, since the new variables are supplied by the sender and an override that does not use them ignores them.
- Idempotence — right. A second reset reads only enabled apps and active credentials, finds none, writes nothing and counts zero; an app disabled before the reset is neither written nor named. A credential revoked between the read and the revoke is not counted (`already_revoked` / `not_found`).
- Concurrent re-enable — right. Each pass re-reads until a read answers none; a row this run already ended that reads live again raises an error instead of looping, which reaches the self-service requester and counts in the forced reset's `failed`.
- Absent stores — right. `rowsOrNone` uses `isObjectAbsentError(error, object)` with the object it read; any other failure is thrown. The operator's command registers both objects (`authIdentityObjects` holds `SysOauthApplication` and `SysScimConnectionCredential`), so there an unregistered-object answer cannot stand in for rows that exist.
- The notice — right on content. It goes to the account's own stored address, carries counts, app names, connection ids with labels, SSO provider ids and a 0/1 second-factor count; no secret, digest, token hint or client id of another account's row is read into it. It is sent only after the arm returned, and both the read for it and the send are caught and logged at warn.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/cli`, under a `fix(plugin-auth)!` title with a BREAKING FROM/TO block and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both the PR body and the changeset. The four packages are exactly the four whose published source the diff touches (`objectql` and `qa` change tests only; `@objectstack/types` is not touched, `isObjectAbsentError` already ships). A behaviour narrowing shipped as a patch with the breaking marker and a FROM/TO is this repo's established shape for a fix of this kind. The `adr-0087: not-required` line holds: no schema key is added, removed or re-shaped. `Check Changeset` concluded success. The level matches what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag — should the administrator's forced reset also mail the account? The seat ruled A: keep as shipped. Judged: the ruling holds against the code. The forced reset has a requester who is answered (`data.revoked`) and a ledger row that records the counts, and it never mailed the account before this PR; the operator's command runs with no mail service at all. One limit follows and is stated in the docs hunk, not hidden: the forced paths report counts, not names, so the administrator finds the rows through the Disabled view and the credential list.
- SQL push-down — no finding. Both reads are indexed equality reads on `user_id` with the flag in the `where`; nothing is joined in the application and no id set is materialised to feed a second query. The writes are one per row through the same single-row doors an administrator uses, and the reason is in the code: each row is named into the tally as it lands, so a later failure still reports what was ended, and the credential write goes through the one revoke function.
- Tenant-audit census — the regenerated count file adds exactly one write call site (`forced-reset-revocation.ts`, `update`), which is the adapter the diff adds.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — in the self-service arm the new registrations step sits ahead of the API-key revocation and is not isolated from it. `endWhatTheAccountAddedBeforeAReset` awaits `endWhatTheAccountRegistered` and only then reaches the `sys_api_key` loop, so an application write or a credential revoke that throws ends the function before any key is read. Before this change the same reset revoked the keys; with it, a row of the new families that cannot be written leaves every API key of the account unrevoked for that reset, and for every later reset while the row stays unwritable. The arm already applies the right principle one level down (credentials are revoked though an application could not be disabled, first failure thrown after both ran) and the forced path counts each family apart; the self-service path should give the keys the same treatment — run the key loop before the registrations, or collect the registrations failure and throw it after the keys. The requester is told either way (the error reaches them), which is why this does not fail the round; no test pins the keys in the failing-write case. The reset notice is also skipped on that path, so the owner is not told what did land.

N1 (nit) — `activeMintedCredentials` keeps a row only when `active` is `true` or `1`, while the verifier (`scimCredentialIsLive`) admits anything that is not `false`, `0` or null. On a boolean column the two agree; reading the flag with the verifier's own predicate would make the agreement structural.

N2 (nit) — the admin revoke door writes a `scim_credential_revoked` audit row per credential; the reset arm does not, and relies on the objects' `trackHistory` plus, on the forced path, the ledger counts. "As Revoke Credential does" in the changeset is exact for the row and the bearer, not for that audit row.

N3 (nit) — `endRegistrations` adds one to `failed` for the whole arm however many rows did not land, the same convention `endAuthorizedApps` uses; `complete` is false either way.

File by file: `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts` holds against the toggle mount, the SCIM service and the MCP door as cited, with S1. `forced-reset-revocation.ts` — the `findOne` fallback through `find` with `limit: 1` passes the same where and context, and the arm's throw is turned into `failed` while what landed is still counted. `operator-password-reset.ts`, `admin-user-endpoints.ts`, `set-password.ts` — carry the two counts through unchanged. `auth-manager-after-hook.ts` — the notice follows the arm and cannot fail the reset; the change path's send condition now includes the two new lists. `auth-manager*.ts`, `auth-manager-email-sms-delivery.ts` — wiring; the sender never throws. `auth-templates.ts` and `package-scoped-resolution.ts` — the tenth platform-requested name is registered where the other nine are, and the two objectql tests that enumerate the set move with it. Tests: real `AuthManager` over a real engine through the route mount, each claim with a control (another account's app, another administrator's credential for the same connection, an already-disabled app, a reset that does not complete, a routine forced reset).

### ① Derived judgments

- A reset now ends each kind of access on its own — right. `endWhatTheAccountAddedBeforeAReset` runs four arms in turn (`unlinkSignInAccounts`, `endOAuthGrants`, `endWhatTheAccountRegistered`, `revokeApiKeys`), each inside its own catch; the failures are collected and the first is thrown only after the fourth arm returned. No arm's throw can reach another arm's call. Inside the third arm the apps and the credentials are still tried apart, as before. The after-hook awaits the function before it calls the notice, so a reset that throws still answers the requester an error and sends no notice. Each tally is counted as its row lands (`ended.signInAccounts += 1` moved into the loop), so nothing depends on an arm finishing.
- The forced path — right, and unchanged in structure. In `revokeSessionsAndApiKeys` the sessions, the keys and the linked accounts each sit in their own try with per-row catches, and `endAuthorizedApps` and `endRegistrations` each turn a throw into `failed`. The extended test drives both doors with the application write refused and pins the key, the link and the credential ended on each.
- One reading of the `active` flag — right. `scimCredentialIsActive` is now the flag half of `scimCredentialIsLive` and is the predicate used by the reset's row filter and by `revokeScimConnectionCredential`; the three can no longer disagree. The store is still asked for `active: true`; on a boolean column that is the only stored value the predicate holds on, so the query and the predicate select the same rows, and the stated reason for not asking "not false" (null rows) is sound. A reset revokes an expired credential whose flag is on; the change reminder lists only rows `scimCredentialIsLive` admits, which is the stricter and correct reading for "still works".
- Audit row — right. `scimCredentialAuditRow` is the one shape for the admin doors and the reset; the admin door's own writer now builds its row through it, with the same six columns as before, and `ScimCredentialAuditDecisions` is re-exported from its old home so no import breaks. The reset writes one `scim_credential_revoked` row per credential it actually revoked (not for `already_revoked` / `not_found`), naming the account on a self-service reset and `actor.id` on `/admin/set-user-password`. It is skipped when the engine has no `insert` or `getSchema('sys_audit_log')` answers nothing — the same test the door's `objectRegistered` applies — and a refused write is caught and reported, never thrown, so it cannot turn a landed revoke into a failed arm. The operator's command hands no actor and writes none, as it writes none for anything else it ends.
- Public surface — additive only: an optional `auditActorId` on `revokeSessionsAndApiKeys`, an optional fourth parameter on `endWhatTheAccountRegistered`, two new exports from scim-connection-service.ts. No response shape, ledger key or template variable moved.
